text:
mike: FYI ran a canary of int8-raven-v2 on the dedicated canary pool. Toolcall parse failures ~0.8% on the eval set. Failures mostly = JSON missing \"action\" or JSON wrapped in prose.
anna: ugh. are these across all sequence lengths or concentrated?
brian: quick grep of failing traces -> lots of them end with truncated '"arguments"' or stray commas before closing brace. looks like token cutoff.
sophie: i suspect KV prefix growth + batching changed the token layout. If prefix pushes model to cut earlier, toolcall JSON can get clipped. saw this before with kvprefix + long system prompts.
mike: exact error snippets: 
```
ParseError: expected key \"action\" but found text
Model output:
\"{\\\"action\\\":\\\"search\\\", \\\"arguments\\\": {\\\"query\\\": \\\"how to optimize batching\\\"}, extra text at end\"
```
anna: interesting — extra trailing prose. could be temperature / decoding leading to commentary after json. what temp was the canary run at?
mike: temp=0.0 default, topk/top_p disabled. deterministic-ish. but under int8 we saw more mid-output hallucinations.
brian: two quick ideas: 1) add a post-gen strict-trim to last brace detection and attempt parse rescue (short regex fix) 2) add an upstream heuristic to detect kvcache-induced truncation by measuring prefix token length distribution and failing fast for short resp lengths.
devon: for the eval harness: we should add a synthetic-prefix test where we prepend 1-3 long kvcache-like prefixes and assert structured output survives. currently harness only tests empty-prefix cases.
sophie: can we test whether continuous batching merges prefixes causing the model to forget where JSON started? maybe some batched requests have shared prefix tokens due to packing. we should repro with batch size=1 vs 8.
anna: also check the model's eos token handling in int8 build. quant rounding sometimes maps eos to a close-but-not-eos token. if eos not respected, model emits extra prose.
mike: good point. logs show slightly different token-id sequences in int8 vs fp16 near the tail.
ci-bot: canary job: https://canaries.internal/runs/2105432100 — attached logs + failing examples.
ops-bot: note: canary pool was running kernel v1.14 on nodes, we rolled a micropatch earlier that changed cudnn params. could be correlated.
brian: incremental mitigation I can push today: implement a small \"json_wrap_rescue\" that tries: (1) find first '{' after start token, (2) find last matching '}' within last 128 tokens, (3) if found, return that substring as JSON candidate and attempt parse. should cut most truncation cases without changing model.
anna: yes but make it opt-in by default for canaries only. we don't want to mask real regressions for customers.
devon: for the long-term: add a metric in rollout that tracks 'json_repair_rate' and surface it in console per-model/version/quantization. makes regressions visible.
sophie: also add a unit test that mutates outputs to include trailing commentary and verifies our rescue heuristics don't accidentally produce wrong structured semantics. e.g. ensure rescued JSON still contains expected keys and types.
mike: plan: 1) enable json_wrap_rescue in canary only (brian) 2) augment eval harness with kv-heavy prefixes + batch-size sweep (devon + sophie) 3) run canary after kernel rollback (ops) 4) add json_repair_rate metric to rollouts (anna)
brian: will open a PR in ~2h. quick patch will include fallback predicate: only try rescue when model_confidence < threshold OR JSON parse fails and output length > minimal.
anna: add a couple failing examples to the PR so CI covers it.
ci-bot: test summary for current run -> parsing_fails: 0.83%, rescue_candidate_count: 12, sample_fail_examples attached.
ops-bot: rolling kernel rollback scheduled in 30m on canary nodes.
devon: after we have more canary runs, let's schedule a day to quantify how much of the increase was int8 vs infra. will run parallel fp16 canary to compare.
sophie: one more note — watch for model-context window mismatch: if backend uses 4k tokens of allocation but tokenizer thinks 3.9k, rounding differences on int8 libs can matter. add debug tokencounts in the harness.
mike: thanks all. small wins first, but please don't hotfix rescue to prod without product signoff. would confuse customers.
anna: ack. will coordinate with product when we have clear delta and postmortem. :thumbsup:
